drhp.business: The Company is principally engaged in the manufacture and marketing of cotton yarn. Its spinning units are situated between Rajkot and Jamnagar, a prominent cotton-producing region in Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles. The Company is engaged in manufacturing of only one product, i.e. cotton yarn, and hence reports a single segment; the secretarial auditor describes the business as manufacturing of varied cotton yarn from raw cotton.

risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns states that fluctuations in cotton prices, availability, quality and exchange rates may materially affect production costs, inventory values and profitability; the Threats section adds that volatility in domestic and international cotton prices may adversely affect raw-material costs, inventory valuation and operating margins. For a pure spinner, cotton is the dominant cost line and the pass-through to yarn realisations is not automatic - the Chairman attributes the year's fall in profitability to fluctuation in profit margins despite turnover growth.
risks.risk: Cotton price, availability and quality volatility (with exchange-rate movement)

risks.note: The Company states that dependence on seasonal cotton procurement exposes it to supply-chain disruption, stock-holding and price-mismatch risks, and that seasonal arrivals may result in higher working-capital requirements. This is structural for a mill that must build cotton stock in the arrival season and carry it, and it showed up in the year: inventory holding days rose from 36.28 days to 40.92 days and the inventory turnover ratio fell to 8.92 times from 10.06 times.
risks.risk: Dependence on seasonal cotton arrivals - procurement, inventory and working-capital risk

risks.note: MD&A flags that uncertainty arising from global tariffs and changing international demand may impact cotton-yarn exports and selling prices, and that global tariff-related issues and uncertainty in major export markets may affect demand and yarn realisations. The Company earns and spends foreign exchange (foreign exchange expenditure of Rs. 4,71,45,463 during the year), so both the demand side and input side are exposed.
risks.risk: Export demand and global tariff uncertainty compressing yarn realisations

risks.note: The Company states that increasing power, labour, finance and compliance costs may exert pressure on operating margins and working-capital requirements, and that fluctuations in these inputs may reduce the competitiveness of spinning units. Spinning is power-intensive; the only stated mitigation is a strict control system to monitor day-to-day power consumption, with no captive generation or energy capex disclosed.
risks.risk: Input-cost inflation in power, labour, finance and compliance costs

risks.note: MD&A states that competition from domestic manufacturers, overseas suppliers and man-made fibres may affect capacity utilisation, market share and product realisations, and that competition from other cotton-producing countries and alternative fibres may pressure export volumes and product margins. Commodity cotton yarn offers little product differentiation, so utilisation and realisation are set largely by the market.
risks.risk: Competition from domestic mills, overseas suppliers and man-made fibres

risks.note: The Company is engaged in manufacturing of only one product, cotton yarn, and hence reports a single segment; all capacity sits in one unit at Haripar, Tal. Kalavad, Dist. Jamnagar, Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles, and there are no subsidiaries, joint ventures or associates. There is no product, geographic or entity diversification to absorb a cotton-cycle downturn or a disruption at the single site, and the Company incurred no research and development expenditure and imported no technology during the year.

Two ordinary resolutions seek omnibus approval for material related party transactions of up to Rs. 100 crore each for FY 2026-27, with Haripriya Spinning Mill Private Limited and Murlidhar Worldtrade Private Limited - both cotton-yarn manufacturers in which the promoters and promoter group indirectly hold substantial shareholding. The Murlidhar proposal alone equals 47.27% of the listed entity's annual consolidated turnover for the immediately preceding financial year and 210.28% of that related party's own turnover. All executive directors, promoters and the entire promoter group are interested and must abstain from voting, so pricing and volume discipline rests on the arm's-length representation and Audit Committee review rather than on independent counterparties.
risks.risk: Scale of promoter-linked related-party trade in the same line of business

risks.note: The Secretarial Audit Report (Form MR-3) records that two e-forms (MGT-15 and DIR-12) were filed late with additional fees, that the outcome of the 6 November 2025 Board meeting was uploaded 26 minutes beyond the three-hour Regulation 30 deadline, and that AGM voting results were submitted one day late, for which BSE imposed and the Company paid a penalty of Rs. 10,000 under Regulation 44(3). A separate FY 2024-25 fine over an allegedly modified audit report led BSE to freeze the promoters' demat accounts until the fine was waived and de-freezing directed during FY 2025-26 - a reminder that compliance slips at this company have previously escalated to promoter-shareholding consequences.
